rationale: All runs are limited by an I/O-port path; reg-to-reg needs only ~4.2-5.2 ns and setup slack stays huge, so setup repair never engages. Subtracting an assumed I/O delay of 20% of target (scales with period), the port path costs ~3.85 ns with timing-driven placement (bm64, aes) versus 5.2-6.0 ns without, and ~0.4 ns less when slew margin >=30% (~70 extra repair buffers). So: minimum period_frac 0.45 to shrink the I/O budget (predicts T_eff ~6.2), timing-driven placement, no routability spreading, post-GRT design repair, slew margin 40, low utilisation (util 38-40 runs failed). Setting 1 refines bm64; setting 2 tests DELAY 4 with ABC buffering, cap213 wires and stronger cap margin.
